Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through the Finova use case and traffic profile. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your SLOs validated and an initial cost/architecture estimate over the next week: 

Recap from the call:
- Target latency: p95 token latency target for short prompts (<=512 tokens) and longer batch workloads. You mentioned wanting sub-200ms p95 for interactive flows.
- Throughput & concurrency: you called out ~500 QPS aggregate and ~2k concurrent sessions at peak across regions.
- Streaming: streaming (partial/real-time tokens) is required for the customer-facing chat UI.
- Regional routing / residency: need EU data residency for EU customers, and multi-region routing (US/EU/APAC) with region-aware failover.

What we need from you to finalize numbers: 
- Traffic histogram (QPS by hour / region) and sample payload sizes (avg & 95th token lengths).
- Confirmation of strict data residency boundaries (e.g., EU must stay in EU region at rest and in transit to EU-only endpoints).
- Any regulatory/compliance constraints beyond SOC2 (e.g., data residency proof, audit windows).

Action items / next steps (for us):
- Attach: redwood-slo-matrix.pdf (SLO mapping template) and multi-region-benchmarks.csv (representative bench results).
- Internal: loop in infra for streaming & concurrency tuning (cc'd Nikhil & Aditya).

Proposed timing: please send the traffic histogram + sample payloads and we'll schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive next week to confirm architecture and initial SOW.

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side and answers to your asks: 

Traffic & targets (current thinking):
- Latency: target ~p95 < 200ms for interactive flows for prompts up to 512 tokens. For longer generations (>=2k tokens) we care more about steady streaming throughput and p99 budgets.
- Throughput / concurrency: expected steady-state ~300 QPS, with peaks up to ~500 QPS global. Peak concurrent live sessions estimate ~1800-2200 (depends on simulation).
- Streaming: yes, streaming is required; our UI relies on partial tokens. Low-latency first-byte is critical.
- Regional routing / data residency: EU customer interactions and logs must remain in-region (EU). US customers can be in US. APAC is lower priority initially but should be supported for failover/routing.

- How does regional pinning work with streaming websockets and fallback if a region is degraded?

Marissa — quick tech note below you can share verbatim with Finova.

Short answer: yes — we can meet the interactive p95 ~200ms target at 512 tokens with the right config and on dedicated capacity; hosted API can approach that for lower concurrency but we recommend Dedicated for predictable p95 at 2k concurrency.

Recommended config (summary):
- Model variant: quantized 8-bit LLM variant (Q8) tuned for inference with attention optimizations.
- Deployment: Dedicated regional pools (US / EU / APAC) with regional pinning for EU traffic. Dedicated ensures predictable tail latencies under high concurrency.
- Autoscale: keep a warm reserve (~20% of peak) + burstable capacity. Configure continuous batching windows tuned to latency SLOs (short window for interactive flows).
- Batching & KV caching: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated context across sessions to reduce token compute. Use smaller batch sizes for interactive low-latency traffic and larger batches for background bulk jobs.
- Streaming: supported via websocket chunked delivery; we support server-sent partial tokens with first-byte optimizations. Keepalive + HTTP/2 or websockets recommended.
- Multi-region failover: requests are routed by policy. For residency-bound traffic, we pin region and only failover to other regions for stateless fallbacks — logs and persisted data remain in-region (via Dedicated or Private).

Expected perf (ballpark, per region, on Dedicated pools):
- Short interactive (<=512 tokens): p50 ~40-80ms, p95 ~120-200ms, p99 ~300-420ms (depends on exact model size and tokenization).
- Longer streaming (>1k tokens): first-byte latency similar; overall completion time scales linearly with token rate.

Notes / risks:
- Hosted multi-tenant environments can hit increased tail latency at sustained 2k concurrency; Dedicated recommended for strict SLOs.
- Data residency: to guarantee EU-only residency for logs/metrics we recommend either Redwood Dedicated provisioned in EU region or our Private deployment option with customer-controlled KMS.

Next asks for Finova (to refine numbers):
- Provide traffic hist by region + sample payloads (avg/95th token lengths).
- Clarify whether logs/audit trails must remain in-region or if anonymized telemetry is ok to cross-region.

I'll produce a 1-page tech note with the above and an initial cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated by EOD tomorrow.
